model.arithmetic: JavaScript Math.fround model of canonical binary32 multiply/add/sqrt/divide and adjacent-value interval expansion
model.group_ball_bound: centroid plus verified-or-synthetically-known L2 radius; Cauchy-Schwarz dot interval; reverse-triangle norm interval; gamma_n plus subnormal eta error envelope

experiments.interpretation: Coordinate-wise extrema were conservative in this random high-dimensional control but too loose to prune a group.

experiments.data_generation: Random normalized group centers; per-coordinate member perturbation bounded by 0.0008/sqrt(D); independent random normalized query; top_k=10.
experiments.interpretation: A very tight synthetic cluster workload showed high theoretical payload selectivity. This is not representative of a measured HME corpus and does not measure bytes, page reads or latency.
No score escaped the modeled interval. Near-zero/ambiguous cases deliberately fell back to [-1,1].

claim_boundary: These are mathematical and binary32 simulation checks, not Rust tests.
The clustered data are deliberately easy to separate and do not establish typical HME workload selectivity.
The centroid radius was computed from synthetic source members in the JS model, not via the production Rust residual verifier.
A simulated group payload fraction is not a measured storage byte/page/latency saving.
A zero-escape finite experiment is not a formal proof of the f32 error envelope.
No ExactComplete, production certificate, SOTA or throughput claim follows.
